proof_scope.completed_class: All bijective token-destination permutations on finite double-star trees are covered by the proved polynomial-time R <= 2 * LB_hub <= 2 * OPT construction.
proof_scope.open_scope: The broader arbitrary-tree approximation problem and extensions beyond double-stars remain open.
proof_scope.proof_scope_not_closed_semantics: This legacy umbrella flag refers only to the broader unrestricted research problem; it does not indicate a gap in the declared double-star theorem.

sources_and_data.data_used: No experimental data. The result is a direct mathematical proof for finite double-star trees with a bijective token-to-destination map.

method: Partition the double-star at its unique central edge. Prepare each center to hold a token destined across that edge, swap the centers, and repeat until all tokens are on their target side. Then decompose each of the two residual star permutations into center-containing and leaf-only cycles and execute explicit star-transposition words. Left and right operations are synchronized only across disjoint vertex sets.
mathematical_claim: For every finite double-star T with adjacent centers u,v, any leaf sets L,R, one distinct token at each vertex, and any bijection from tokens to destination vertices, the construction uses R <= 2r + 2 max(a,b) = 2 max(W(u),W(v)) <= 2 LB_hub(T,pi) <= 2 OPT(T,pi) matching rounds, where r is the number of A-to-B tokens for A=L∪{u}, B=R∪{v}; a,b are initially incorrect leaves; W(x)=sum_{e incident x} C(e)/2; and LB_hub=max(D,max_x W(x)). It is a constructive polynomial-time 2-approximation on double-stars only.
assumptions: T is a finite tree with exactly two adjacent centers u,v and all other vertices are leaves adjacent to one center; either leaf set may be empty.
Each vertex contains exactly one distinct token and each token has exactly one destination, with the destination assignment a bijection on V(T).
A round consists of swaps on a matching of T edges; no vertex participates in two swaps in one round.
C(e) counts source-to-destination token paths using e; tree-cut balance makes C(e) even and r(e)=C(e)/2 integral.
LB_hub is the maximum of maximum token distance D and the mandatory incident-edge workload W(x)=sum_{e incident x} r(e).
verified_steps: Bijection gives equal directional transfer counts across the central cut; this common count is r.
Before each central swap, if a center lacks an outward token, a leaf in its side must hold one; the two possible preparation edges are disjoint.
Each central swap exchanges one outward token in each direction, decreasing both remaining counts by one.
No initially correct leaf is prepared; each prepared leaf receives a non-outgoing center token and cannot be used again. Thus post-phase-I incorrect leaf counts are at most a,b.
Center-containing star cycles are sorted with q swaps; leaf-only cycles of size q>=2 are sorted with q+1<=2q swaps while restoring the center token.
The two star vertex sets are disjoint; each side serializes its own center-incident swaps and the two sequences run in parallel.
The edge and hub loads yield W(u)=r+a and W(v)=r+b; adding the phase bounds gives R<=2 LB_hub.
Every round is a matching and all actual token identities are tracked; construction and output size are O(|V|).
gaps: The proof uses the unique central edge to split the graph into two stars; at three or more hubs, overlapping cut-correction states leave a nontrivial backbone and no corresponding bound is proved.
The source audit is bounded and cannot establish global priority or absence of equivalent prior results.
No optimality result for the produced schedule is claimed.

review_checks: center token can be either outward or locally destined
initially correct leaves and one-time leaf preparation
equal directional crossing counts and no stranded outgoing tokens
centers with leaf destinations and center-containing cycles
leaf-only cycles and restoration of the center token
disjoint preparation edges and separation of bridge rounds
synchronized left/right schedules and degenerate empty-leaf side
independent_review.method: Independent token-state induction and separate cycle-by-cycle permutation check; no experiment or finite search was run.

novelty_assessment.closest_parallel_prior_art: polynomial approximation for one-junction subdivided stars; genuine double-stars with both centers branching are outside that class, although degenerate double-stars may overlap
novelty_assessment.double_broom_prior_art: optimal sequential swap objective, not parallel matching rounds

next_falsifiable_action: For three adjacent hubs with arbitrary pendant leaves and permutations, determine whether any sequential cut-correction normal form preserves the double-star phase invariant; exhibit the exact shared-center dependency if it fails. Proof-only; no experiment authorization is requested.
observed_result_or_blocker: The proposed double-star construction is valid for all bijective destination permutations and gives a polynomial-time 2-approximation relative to LB_hub. Extension fails at the proof-decomposition level because a middle hub lies on two backbone cuts; this is an unresolved generalization issue, not a counterexample.
uncertainty: Whether a stronger or simpler known double-star parallel theorem exists beyond the bounded primary-source audit.
Whether a comparable LB_hub-relative schedule can be proved for three or more hubs or arbitrary trees.
Whether the factor 2 is improvable on double-stars.
